Study_Title: Janus: Evidence-Before-Effect Sagas and Offline-Verifiable Provenance for Agentic LLMs
Threat_Attacker_Model: Process crash or daemon kill between effect execution and log persistence; unauthenticated or self-approved tool execution; history rewriting or unverified log export in financial LLM workflows.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: CBOR envelopes in a BLAKE3 hash-chained append-only log; RFC 6962/9162 Merkle tree roots per segment signed with Ed25519; participant answers/proposals signed with manifest-pinned Ed25519 keys.
Enforcement_Point_Location: janus-orchd saga orchestrator daemon, MCP proxy interceptor, pure-function gate evaluator, transactional outbox, and offline janus-verify auditor.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Evidence-Before-Effect invariant (proposal, gate verdict, and signed validator/human answer durably committed before tool effect release); offline-verifiable provenance across 8 invariants.
Trust_Assumptions: Ed25519 private keys of registered participants and the janus-orchd operator host are not compromised; BLAKE3 and Ed25519 are collision/forgery resistant (no external blockchain anchor against operator history rewrite).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Single-node throughput: 83,765 events/s at p99 0.97 ms (64 producers), 215,400 events/s at p99 3.06 ms (256 producers), 315,106 events/s at 1,024 producers; gated step median latency 5.39 ms (concurrency 1) and 13.46 ms (concurrency 8, 2,000 sagas); pure gate evaluation 0.01–0.02 ms; offline janus-verify verifies 100M events in 254.5 s; 0 invariant violations across 225 crash-injection kills (144 in-process, 81 daemon) (pp. 1, 6–8, Table III).
Exposed_Security_Function: Pre-effect synchronous saga logging, Ed25519 manifest-pinned answer verification, and offline Merkle-segment auditing.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical Ed25519 signatures (vulnerable to quantum Shor's algorithm); lacks external transparency-log witnessing against a malicious operator rewriting its entire local log tail (§III-C, p. 3); evaluated on single-host Linux NVMe.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. IV–VI (pp. 1, 4–8, Table II–III): 'A step's proposal, the verdict on it and any answer from a validator or a person are durable in a signed, hash-chained log before the step may run or its effect be released... We evaluate Janus under crash injection (144 kills in-process, 81 through the daemon), by verifying a 100-million-event log offline (254.5 s)...'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Janus enforces an Evidence-Before-Effect saga architecture using BLAKE3 hash chains and Ed25519-signed RFC 6962 Merkle segments, achieving 83,765 events/s (p99 0.97 ms), 5.39 ms median gated-step latency, 254.5 s offline verification of 100M events, and zero invariant violations across 225 crash-injection tests.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 13-page systems paper with formal 8-invariant state machine (Lemma 1, Table II), crash-fault injection (225 kills), 100M-event offline audit benchmark, and recorded-model lending workflow evaluation.
Protected_Object: Tool execution proposals, gate verdicts, human/validator Ed25519-signed approvals, and CBOR/BLAKE3/Merkle evidence log segments.
Composition_Evidence: Composes MCP proxy interception (B1/B2), pure-function gate evaluation & outbox release (B3), and BLAKE3+Ed25519 Merkle segment verification (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-337 / ARXIV-S-0263) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3;B4); Bukti=FORMAL_MODEL; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (DG;AD).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi adjudikasi lintas-reviewer Stage 3.

Security_Property_Guaranteed: Zero split-brain invariant violations across 225 crash-injection kills and linear-time offline cryptographic verification of 100M events.

Study_Title: Delegation Without Trust: An Empirical Gap Analysis of Identity, Authorization, and Runtime Governance in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Confused deputy escalation, bearer-token exfiltration/replay, cross-agent privilege amplification, and forged or unattenuated sub-agent delegation across multi-agent LLM frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Macaroon-style HMAC-SHA256 chained capability tokens with monotonic Datalog caveat attenuation, workload-identity binding (SPIFFE/DPoP style), and short-lived per-invocation issuance.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Model-independent Reference Capability Broker mediating all inter-agent delegation and tool-server invocations outside the LLM context.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Monotonic privilege attenuation across multi-hop sub-agent delegation; zero forged-token acceptance; strict task-scoped blast-radius containment under sub-agent compromise.
Trust_Assumptions: Reference capability broker and root HMAC signing secret are isolated from agent LLM processes; Datalog policy rules accurately encode least-privilege task scopes.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Blocks all 4 threat classes across 5 frameworks (Table 1 & 4), resists 11 direct protocol attacks, accepts 0 / 200,000 forged tokens, reduces compromised sub-agent reachable actions from 8,100 (bearer delegation) to a mean of 1.5 actions across 2,000 randomized scenarios, with ~2.6 µs per-decision broker overhead (pp. 1, 5–9).
Exposed_Security_Function: HMAC-chained capability token minting, Datalog caveat attenuation, and model-external reference monitor enforcement.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Uses symmetric HMAC-SHA256 macaroon chains requiring a trusted central broker rather than decentralized asymmetric non-repudiation; policy synthesis from natural-language user intent remains manual.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 3–6 (pp. 1, 5–9, Tables 1–4): 'It blocks all four threats; it resists 11 direct attacks on its own design and accepts 0 of 200,000 forged tokens; it confines a compromised sub-agent to its delegated task (a mean of 1.5 reachable actions versus all 8,100 under bearer delegation, across 2,000 randomized scenarios); and it enforces at microsecond cost (~2.6 µs per decision)...'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Empirical gap analysis shows 5 major agent frameworks fail 8 delegation security requirements under default bearer tokens, whereas a model-independent HMAC-chained Datalog capability broker blocks all 4 threat classes, rejects 200,000/200,000 forged tokens, and shrinks compromised sub-agent reachability from 8,100 to 1.5 actions at ~2.6 µs per decision.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 14-page empirical gap analysis across 5 agent frameworks and 6 standards (OAuth 2.1, RFC 8693, SPIFFE, Macaroons/Biscuits, MCP) paired with a 2,000-scenario capability-broker benchmark.
Protected_Object: Sub-agent delegation tokens, Datalog attenuation caveats, workload identities, and downstream tool invocations.
Composition_Evidence: Enforces monotonic attenuation from user intent (B1) through sub-agent token exchange (B2) to runtime tool reference monitoring (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-338 / ARXIV-S-0266) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3); Bukti=FORMAL_MODEL; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (AD;UG).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi adjudikasi lintas-reviewer Stage 3.

Study_Title: Delegation Without Trust: An Empirical Gap Analysis of Identity, Authorization, and Runtime Governance in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Default bearer-token delegation gaps across 5 production multi-agent frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, and MCP OAuth 2.1 profile) enabling cross-agent privilege escalation and full 8,100-action blast radius exposure.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Comparative standards matrix auditing OAuth 2.1, OAuth Token Exchange (RFC 8693), Resource Indicators (RFC 8707), SPIFFE/mTLS, DPoP, and Macaroons/Biscuits against 8 agent delegation requirements (`R1`–`R8`).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Framework-level Delegation & Credential Passing Layer across 5 evaluated multi-agent runtimes.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that 0/5 agent frameworks and 0/6 individual standards satisfy all 8 delegation security requirements (`R1`–`R8`) out of the box.
Trust_Assumptions: Default framework configurations documented in official releases represent typical developer deployments.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Audits 5 frameworks against 4 threat classes (`T1`–`T4`) and 8 requirements (`R1`–`R8`, Tables 1–3, pp. 5–6): 3 frameworks provide zero delegation controls, MCP's OAuth 2.1 + RFC 8707 profile provides only partial coverage (`R3`, `R4`, `R6`, `R8` but lacks `R1` provenance and `R2` sub-agent attenuation), and compromised sub-agents under default bearer delegation reach all 8,100 actions across 2,000 scenarios (p. 1, 7).
Exposed_Security_Function: Empirical vulnerability and requirement-coverage matrix across 5 agent frameworks and 6 authentication standards.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluates default framework configurations; custom enterprise wrappers can manually combine RFC 8693, DPoP/mTLS, and external policy engines.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 3–4 (pp. 5–6, Tables 1–3): 'Three frameworks provide none; MCP's OAuth model gives partial coverage... First, no single standard covers the requirement set: delegation provenance (R1) and attenuation (R2) live in token-exchange and capability tokens; sender-constraining (R3) and rotation (R5) live in SPIFFE/mTLS/DPoP; model-independent enforcement (R8) is a deployment property none of them mandates.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Empirical audit of 5 multi-agent frameworks and 6 security standards (OAuth 2.1, RFC 8693, RFC 8707, SPIFFE/mTLS, DPoP, Macaroons) proves that no single framework or standard satisfies all 8 agent delegation requirements (`R1`–`R8`), leaving all 8,100 actions exposed under default bearer delegation.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Standards and framework gap analysis in Section 3–4 (Tables 1–3) of ARXIV-S-0266.
Protected_Object: OAuth 2.1 tokens, RFC 8693 token exchange payloads, SPIFFE/mTLS identities, and multi-agent framework runtimes.
Composition_Evidence: Maps structural gaps across user authentication (B1), sub-agent token attenuation (B2), and model-independent tool enforcement (B3).

Study_Title: BlockA2A: Towards Secure and Verifiable Agent-to-Agent Interoperability
Threat_Attacker_Model: Cross-MAS identity spoofing, unauthorized capability invocation, Byzantine agent collusion, replay attacks, and tamper-prone off-chain interaction logs in heterogeneous multi-agent systems.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) with SHA-256 document hashes, Access Control Contracts (ACC), BLS multi-signatures for consensus, Merkle trees for batch audit verification, and 2-party computation (2PC) with HMAC integrity checks.
Enforcement_Point_Location: BlockA2A Decentralized Identity & Access Control Contract (ACC) layer, Dynamic Threat Evaluation (DTE) & Defense Orchestration Engine (DOE), and Blockchain Ledger layer.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cross-MAS Trust Equivalence (Theorem 1), cryptographic non-repudiation of inter-agent task handoffs, replay resistance within validity window tau_max, and sub-second automated Byzantine threat neutralization.
Trust_Assumptions: Blockchain consensus quorum (BLS multi-signature validators) is honest above Byzantine threshold; agent DID private keys are securely stored.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Core cryptographic and DID/ACC operations complete in <10 ms on average (64.0 ms for on-chain state transitions, Table 2, p. 38); DOE counter-attack algorithms neutralize Byzantine/spoofing attacks within ~110 ms across 10-run averages (Table 3, pp. 38–39).
Exposed_Security_Function: On-chain DID registration, Smart-Contract Access Control (ACC), BLS multi-signature Merkle anchoring, and DOE automated counter-attack orchestration.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on pre-quantum BLS multi-signatures, SHA-256, and HMAC (vulnerable to quantum Shor's algorithm on BLS); on-chain state transition latency (64.0 ms) and gas costs depend on underlying permissioned/consortium chain throughput.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 3 & Sec. 5–6 (pp. 8–19, 31, 37–39, Theorem 1, Tables 1–3): 'Cryptographic Primitives: SHA-256 for hashing, BLS multi-signatures for consensus, and Merkle trees for batch verification... The trust preservation is guaranteed by the Cross-MAS Trust Equivalence Theorem (Theorem 1)... All three counter-attack algorithms complete within ~110ms...'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: BlockA2A secures cross-MAS agent interoperability via W3C DIDs, smart-contract Access Control Contracts (ACC), BLS multi-signatures, and Merkle-anchored ledgers, proving Cross-MAS Trust Equivalence (Theorem 1) with <10 ms core verification latency, 64.0 ms state transitions, and ~110 ms active threat neutralization.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 42-page architectural and formal paper proving Theorem 1 (Cross-MAS Trust Equivalence) and benchmarking DID/ACC/DOE latency across simulated multi-agent attacks.
Protected_Object: Agent DID documents, cross-MAS task parameters (H_task), ACC access policies, and Merkle-anchored interaction logs.
Composition_Evidence: Binds decentralized agent identity and ACC authorization (B2) to 2PC/HMAC data retrieval (B3) and BLS/Merkle ledger auditing (B4).

Study_Title: Don't believe everything you read: Understanding and Measuring MCP Behavior under Misleading Tool Descriptions
Threat_Attacker_Model: Description-to-code inconsistency and misleading tool descriptions in third-party MCP servers enabling covert network calls, undeclared file/environment access, and privilege escalation.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Static AST code-path extraction paired with LLM semantic alignment auditing comparing declared MCP tool descriptions against actual Python/TypeScript implementation behaviors.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Pre-deployment MCP Registry & Pre-invocation Static-Semantic Consistency Auditor.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Detection and quantification of description-behavior mismatches (Full Match, Partial Match, Mismatch) across real-world MCP tool implementations.
Trust_Assumptions: Server source code inspected in the repository matches the deployed MCP server package.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 10,222 MCP tools from real-world servers, only ~53.5% (4,202/7,858 in the 0–9 star bin) achieve Full Match between description and code; in Developer Tools and Productivity categories, Full Match is 53.2% and 45.0% (41.5% in lower-ranked categories), and Full Match drops inversely with popularity from 53.5% (0–9 stars) to 47.7% (10–99), 44.1% (100–999), and 29.1% (1,000–9,999 stars) (pp. 4–6, Tables 1–3).
Exposed_Security_Function: Cross-checking natural-language MCP tool metadata against static code execution behavior.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Static AST + LLM consistency analysis can miss dynamically fetched payloads or obfuscated native binaries; does not provide a cryptographic runtime enforcement sandbox.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. IV–V (pp. 4–6, Tables 1–3): 'Table 1: Consistency Levels by Category... Developer Tools and Productivity have the largest tool counts, but their Full Match rates are approximately 53.2% and 45.0%... The proportion of Full Match shows an inverse trend with popularity: 53.5% (4,202/7,858) in 0–9 stars, 47.7% (894/1,874) in 10–99, 44.1% (178/404) in 100–999, and 29.1% (25/86) in 1000–9999.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Empirical measurement of real-world MCP servers reveals pervasive description-to-implementation inconsistency: only 45.0%–53.2% of tools in major categories fully match their declared behavior, and Full Match declines from 53.5% in low-star repos to 29.1% in highly popular (1,000–9,999 star) repositories.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 8-page empirical measurement study analyzing description-vs-implementation consistency across categories, popularity tiers, and download sources in the MCP ecosystem.
Protected_Object: MCP tool natural-language descriptions, input schemas, and underlying server source code.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates how metadata deception at tool discovery (B1/B2) induces unauthorized code execution and side effects (B3/B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-341 / ARXIV-S-0272) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3;B4); Bukti=INFORMAL_ARGUMENT; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=NOT_DISCUSSED; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (AD;UG).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi adjudikasi lintas-reviewer Stage 3.

Study_Title: Registry Descriptions Go Stale Unevenly: An 89-Day Measurement of Model Context Protocol Drift, and Why Drift-Ranked Re-Auditing Under-Covers It
Threat_Attacker_Model: Stale static security audit verdicts on MCP registries caused by silent post-audit server metadata/description mutations ('rug pulls' and uneven registry drift) that evade drift-ranked re-auditing.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Canonicalized SHA-256 content digests over full server descriptors (`f = SHA-256(descriptor)`) and isolated description text (`d = SHA-256(description)`) with delta-encoded revision tracking.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Longitudinal MCP Registry Auditor & Continuous Content-Hash Revalidation Pipeline.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Exact detection of post-audit description drift and quantification of survival/staleness curves and re-audit under-coverage across live MCP registries.
Trust_Assumptions: Registry snapshots and SHA-256 digests are recorded faithfully at each observation epoch.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: 89-day longitudinal measurement across live MCP registry cohorts: 75.2% of servers never change (delta encoding compresses 51 MB of SHA-256 digests to 1.3 MB), 19.1% drift by day 89 (vs. 73% under naive daily rate compounding — a ~3.8x overestimate), live change load is 38.7 events/day (2.04 per 1,000 entries/day), and prior description change lifts next-period drift probability 4.8x (7.1x in H1) but covers only 5% of servers, causing drift-ranked re-auditing to under-cover first-time mutations (pp. 1–10).
Exposed_Security_Function: SHA-256 descriptor/description hashing, Kaplan-Meier survival estimation, and registry re-audit scheduling analysis.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Scoped strictly to registry-published metadata and description text (`d = SHA-256`); does not probe live MCP server `tools/list` runtime responses or underlying code changes that leave registry descriptions untouched (§7, p. 11).

Study_Title: The Decomposition Is the Fingerprint: Per-Component Identity for Agent Skills

Study_Title: Agent-Native Telemetry: Verifiable State-Delta Evidence for Autonomous Operations

Study_Title: RAILS: Verification-Native Clearing For Agentic Commerce
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unverified obligation fulfillment in agentic commerce, single-judge LLM false clears (43.3%–96.7% on defective work), `FORGE-UP` evidence fabrication, and `LAUNDER-BASIS` verifier collusion across MCP, A2A, AP2, and x402 payment rails.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Ed25519 digital signatures on obligation envelopes and verifier attestations, SHA-256 32-byte evidence digests, TPM/TEE hardware-backed attestations, and declared-basis (`B_i`) clearing contracts.
Enforcement_Point_Location: RAILS Verification-Native Clearing Engine & Multi-Verifier Mesh mediating settlement instructions (instant release, escrow hold, or dispute escalation).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographic binding between delegated obligations, declared evidence bases (`B_i`), and settlement actions; bounded detection of `LAUNDER-BASIS` collusion and resistance to `FORGE-UP` without key/TEE compromise.
Trust_Assumptions: Ed25519 registrar keys and TEE/TPM hardware roots are uncompromised; a non-zero fraction of audit rounds sample independent higher-tier verifiers.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Demonstrates that single frontier LLM judges suffer 43.3%–96.7% false-clear rates on defective agent work (Mistral Large 86.7%, Gemini 2.5 Flash 96.7%, Gemini 2.5 Pro 43.3%, GPT-5.4 mini 30.0%) while zero-false-clear judges clear only 41.7%–50% of legitimate work (p. 35); RAILS declared-basis clearing cuts unescalated defective work and detects 100% of `LAUNDER-BASIS` collusion with median detection latency dropping from ~547 rounds (at 2% audit rate) to ~46 rounds (at 40% audit rate) (pp. 32–37).
Exposed_Security_Function: Ed25519-signed obligation envelopes, SHA-256 evidence-basis declarations (`B_i`), and multi-tiered randomized clearing audits.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical Ed25519 signatures and SHA-256 digests (`STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY`); collusion detection latency (~46–547 rounds) depends on paid higher-tier audit sampling rates.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 4–5 & Sec. 8–9 (pp. 6, 11, 32–37, 43): 'every judge that clears most legitimate work, above 70%, carries a false-clear rate between 43.3% and 96.7%... A successful FORGE-UP on a Mesh whose ingest verification works requires forging a cryptographic primitive (TLS, an Ed25519 signature, a TPM-backed attestation)... LAUNDER-BASIS collusion was always caught in the end, with median detection latency falling from about 547 audit rounds at a 2% audit rate to about 46 at 40%.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: RAILS resolves the agentic commerce clearing gap across MCP/A2A/AP2/x402 by binding Ed25519-signed obligation envelopes to SHA-256 declared evidence bases (`B_i`), overcoming single-LLM judge false-clear rates (43.3%–96.7%) and catching 100% of `LAUNDER-BASIS` collusion (median 46 rounds at 40% audit rate).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 49-page formal clearing architecture and empirical evaluation across frontier LLM judges (Claude 4.5/4.6/4.8, GPT-5.4/5.5, Gemini 2.5, Mistral Large) and adversarial collusion simulations.
Protected_Object: Delegated commercial obligations, Ed25519-signed execution envelopes, SHA-256 evidence digests, and payment settlement instructions.
Composition_Evidence: Connects obligation mandates (B1/B2) and tool/payment execution receipts (B3) to multi-verifier cryptographic clearing and audit settlement (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-352 / ARXIV-S-0290) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3;B4); Bukti=FORMAL_MODEL; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (DG;AD;UG).

Study_Title: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) embedded in external untrusted data retrieved during tool use, computer use, and coding agent workflows causing unauthorized tool invocations and intent concealment.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: None (large-scale red-teaming competition evaluating 13 frontier proprietary and open-weight LLM agents against dual tool-judge and prompt-judge verifiers).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Model-level safety alignment and runtime tool-call guardrails across 13 evaluated frontier agent models.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Empirical robustness against indirect prompt injection across 37 target harmful behaviors and 3 agentic modalities (Tool Use, Computer Use, Coding).
Trust_Assumptions: Competition evaluation harness and dual tool/prompt judges accurately classify successful harmful actions.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across hundreds of thousands of red-team attempts on 13 frontier models and 37 behaviors, overall Attack Success Rate (ASR) ranges from 0.5% (Claude Opus 4.5 over 12.0k attempts) to 8.5% (Gemini 2.5 Pro over 19.6k attempts); by modality, Tool Use is most vulnerable at 4.82% ASR (95% CI [4.68%, 4.96%]), followed by Computer Use at 3.13% ([2.96%, 3.31%]) and Coding at 2.51% ([2.41%, 2.62%]) (pp. 3, 9–10, Figure 1, Table 2).

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Even the most robust frontier model (Claude Opus 4.5) exhibits non-zero ASR (0.5% overall, 1.1% on Computer Use), confirming that model-level alignment alone cannot guarantee zero IPI exploitation without deterministic execution gates.

Gemini 2.5 Pro exhibited the highest vulnerability (8.5% ASR across 19.6k attempts), while Claude Opus 4.5 showed the strongest robustness (0.5% ASR across 12.0k attempts)... Tool use scenarios were the most vulnerable with an ASR of 4.82%, followed by computer use (3.13%) and coding (2.51%).'

Study_Title: Taming Various Privilege Escalation in LLM-Based Agent Systems: A Mandatory Access Control Framework
Threat_Attacker_Model: Privilege escalation in single- and multi-agent LLM systems (`tau_at` agent-to-tool and `tau_aa` agent-to-agent) driven by indirect prompt injection, RAG poisoning (ASR > 50% on IsolateGPT hub RAG), and over-privileged tool sets.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Mandatory Access Control (MAC) security lattice with taint/integrity labels (`SEMemory` for RAG/memory compartments and `SETool` / `SEAgent` for least-privilege tool/agent transitions, Definitions 1–4).
Enforcement_Point_Location: SEAgent Mandatory Access Control Reference Monitor mediating memory/RAG retrieval (`SEMemory`), inter-agent handoffs, and tool invocations.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Formal prevention of unauthorized privilege escalation (Definitions 1–4) across memory, RAG, inter-agent communication, and tool execution.
Trust_Assumptions: SEAgent MAC reference monitor is non-bypassable and initial task-derived security labels are faithfully initialized.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Eliminates RAG-poisoning and cross-tool privilege escalation (reducing ASR from >50% on Naive/IsolateGPT hub-RAG to 0% on controlled MAC benchmarks) while improving API-Bank task correctness over IsolateGPT (74.73% vs. 53.95% on 1-tool, 71.34% vs. 37.32% on 2-tool, 67.91% vs. 37.25% on >=3-tool) with 0%–5.13% FPR and lower execution latency (9.00–12.79 s vs. 21.98–64.42 s; MAC policy check overhead 3.07–5.86 ms) (pp. 3–4, 10–12, Definitions 1–4, Table 5).
Exposed_Security_Function: Formal MAC state-transition labeling (`SEMemory` + `SEAgent`) enforcing least-privilege information flow across RAG, sub-agents, and tools.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Token overhead increases by ~32%–35% on short-context benchmarks (e.g., 3,558 to 4,810 tokens on API-Bank 1-tool, p. 11) due to MAC system prompt and policy metadata.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 3–6 (pp. 3–4, 10–12, Definitions 1–4, Table 5): 'Definition 4 (Privilege Escalation in Agent Systems)... When the RAG module is used in the Hub component, the ASR can reach more than 50% since its isolation mechanism does not cover RAG data processing... SEAgent Correctness: 74.73% (1 tool), 71.34% (2 tools), 67.91% (>=3 tools); FP Rate: 0% (1–2 tools), 5.13% (>=3 tools); Execution Time: 9.00s–12.79s vs. 21.98s–64.42s for IsolateGPT.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: SEAgent formalizes agent privilege escalation (Definitions 1–4) and enforces Mandatory Access Control across RAG memory (`SEMemory`), sub-agents, and tools, blocking RAG-poisoning escalations (>50% ASR on IsolateGPT) while outperforming IsolateGPT in task correctness (67.91%–74.73% vs. 37.25%–53.95%) and latency (9.0–12.8 s vs. 22.0–64.4 s).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 25-page formal modeling and empirical evaluation paper benchmarking SEAgent against Naive Agent and IsolateGPT on InjecAgent, API-Bank, and multi-agent suites.
Protected_Object: RAG/memory chunks (`SEMemory`), inter-agent messages (`tau_aa`), and tool invocation requests (`tau_at`).
Composition_Evidence: Enforces MAC security labels from user task initialization and RAG retrieval (B1) through inter-agent delegation (B2) to tool execution (B3).

Study_Title: Your Agent Is Mine: Measuring Malicious Intermediary Attacks on the LLM Supply Chain
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious third-party LLM API routers (application-layer MITM proxies) performing active tool-call argument rewriting (`AC-1`), adaptive multi-turn evasion (`AC-1.a`/`AC-1.b`), and passive credential harvesting (`AC-2`) across plaintext JSON tool traffic.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Evaluates 3 defenses: deterministic pre-execution policy gate, statistical anomaly screening, and append-only cryptographic transparency logging (1.26 KB/entry, 12.0 MB/1,000 sessions); notes 0/4 agent frameworks implement end-to-end client-to-model response integrity.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Client-side Tool-Call Policy Gate, Anomaly Screener, and Session Transparency Log.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies real-world credential leakage and buffered-streaming tool-call tampering overhead across 4 major agent frameworks.
Trust_Assumptions: Third-party API routers are untrusted intermediaries with full plaintext access to in-flight OpenAI-compatible JSON payloads.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Honeypot/decoy measurement captured 2B GPT-5.4 / 5.3-codex tokens (~13 GB traffic) from 147 IPs (6 JA3 fingerprints), exposing 99 unique leaked credentials (OpenAI, AWS, GitHub PAT, Slack, Ethereum, PEM keys) across 440 Codex sessions on 398 projects (pp. 2, 5, 8); active `AC-1` rewrite succeeds on 100% (4/4) of frameworks (99.6% `AC-1.a`) with 0.013 ms median proxy overhead (0.004–0.005 ms stream buffer pause vs. 820 ms upstream latency, p. 9); policy gate blocks 100% of static `AC-1`/`AC-1.a` at 2.3 µs (1.0% FP) but suffers 100% adaptive bypass (`AC-1.b`), while transparency logging adds 1.26 KB/entry (12.0 MB/1k sessions, p. 10).
Exposed_Security_Function: In-flight SSE stream buffering/rewriting, regex secret extraction, microsecond policy gating, and session transparency logging.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Static policy gates suffer 100% bypass under adaptive `AC-1.b` attacks (p. 10), and true end-to-end cryptographic response signing requires upstream LLM provider protocol changes.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 4–6 (pp. 2, 8–10, Tables 2–4): 'served roughly 2B GPT-5.4 and 5.3-codex tokens, corresponding to roughly 13 GB of visible downstream prompt/response traffic, and exposed 99 unique credentials across 440 Codex sessions... Per-request proxy overhead is 0.013 ms median over 10,000 requests... Policy gate: 100% AC-1, 1.0% FP; 2.3 µs; 100% adaptive bypass... Transparency log: 12.0 MB/1k sessions; 1.26 KB/entry.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Third-party LLM API routers act as unauthenticated MITM proxies: wild measurement across 2B tokens (13 GB) exposed 99 credentials across 440 Codex sessions, active SSE tool-call rewriting (`AC-1`) succeeds on 4/4 frameworks with 0.013 ms overhead, and local policy gates (2.3 µs) suffer 100% adaptive bypass without transparency logs (1.26 KB/entry).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 16-page wild measurement and systems evaluation across 4 agent frameworks, 10,000 proxy requests, and 440 wild Codex sessions.

Study_Title: MemMark: State-Evolution Attribution Watermarking for Agent Long-Term Memory Systems

Enforcement_Point_Location: MEMMARK Memory-Write Boundary Interceptor & Cryptographic Audit Trace Verifier.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Strict single-step distribution preservation (Lemma 1), multi-step cascade composition soundness (Lemma 2), and unforgeable snapshot-only provenance attribution.

Exposed_Security_Function: Keyed distribution-preserving memory-write watermarking bound to cryptographic commitments and signed per-session Merkle roots.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical Pedersen commitments, Merkle hashes, and digital signatures (`STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY`); extreme memory-wiping attacks that destroy >80% of graph nodes degrade watermark bit capacity.

Study_Title: What Guides the Agent? Adjudicating Unauthorized Behavior via Localizing Behavior-Guiding Instructions
Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect prompt injection where benign-looking instructions embedded in untrusted external tool outputs hijack agent tool invocations without triggering static keyword/perplexity filters.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Attention-based instruction-localization detector (`AttnLocate`) with attention-sink suppression (`beta = 10`) paired with configurable source-authority policies (`Principal-only`, `Tool-authorized`, `Result-authorized`).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Inference-time Attention Localization & Authority-Policy Adjudicator gating agent tool calls.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Fine-grained token-span localization (`mIoU`) of behavior-guiding instructions and deterministic adjudication of whether the instruction originates from an authorized principal or untrusted data.
Trust_Assumptions: White-box access to internal transformer attention weights is available during agent inference; source-segment boundaries (user prompt vs. tool output) are tagged.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Surpasses 0.95 TPR across all detectors on InjecAgent (peaking at 0.989 AUROC and 0.984 TPR on Gemma2-9B; 0.947 TPR and 0.070 FPR on Phi-4 think mode, Table 1–2, p. 6); attention-sink suppression (`beta = 10`) cuts FPR from 0.417 to 0.070 (peak mIoU 0.774, TPR 0.927), and authority-policy adjudication maintains TPR > 0.909 and FPR < 0.086 across all 3 policy tiers (Tables 3–4, p. 7).
Exposed_Security_Function: Attention-weight instruction localization (`AttnLocate`) and source-authority policy adjudication.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Resolved UNMAPPED in DAFTAR_442 to MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3). Requires white-box access to model attention weights (inapplicable to closed commercial APIs), and localization mIoU/TPR degrade on long contexts (>2,048 tokens: mIoU drops from 0.8105 to 0.6951 and TPR from 0.9722 to 0.8571, p. 7).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 4–5 (pp. 5–7, Tables 1–4): 'On InjecAgent, all detectors surpass 0.95 TPR, and Gemma2-9B stands out with an AUROC of 0.989 and a TPR of 0.984... Varying the authority policy... yields stable performance, with TPR above 0.909 and FPR below 0.086.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: AttnLocate localizes behavior-guiding instructions via sink-suppressed attention weights (`beta = 10`, cutting FPR from 0.417 to 0.070) and adjudicates them against configurable authority policies, achieving up to 0.989 AUROC / 0.984 TPR on InjecAgent and >0.909 TPR / <0.086 FPR across authority tiers.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 9-page white-box attention-localization and authority-adjudication study evaluated across multiple open-weight LLM agents and injection benchmarks.
Protected_Object: Untrusted external tool outputs, internal transformer attention maps, and downstream agent tool invocations.
Composition_Evidence: Traces which input segment (B1 user prompt vs. B2 tool result) guides the model's reasoning to authorize or block tool execution (B3).

Study_Title: AUDITA: certified auditing and causal attribution of adverse outcomes in autonomous multi-agent systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: False blame shifting, multi-agent collusion, evidence destruction/omission, and misattribution of overdetermined or preempted adverse outcomes in embodied and software multi-agent fleets.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Author-signed inter-agent messages with causal parent citations, delivery receipts, and epoch-windowed Merkle-tree commitments chained to previous block hashes (`write -> sign -> cite -> receipt -> seal -> store`).
Enforcement_Point_Location: AUDITA Certified Auditing & Two-Layer Counterfactual Causal Attribution Engine.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Non-conviction of rule-following agents (Theorem 1), machine-checkable collusion certificates (Theorem 2), flagged author-attributed uncertainty under evidence destruction (Theorem 3), record-confined completeness barrier (Theorem 4), certificate tamper survival (Theorem 5), and replay-verified soundness (Proposition 1).
Trust_Assumptions: Each principal's signing key is uncompromised; operational duties and replay dynamics for certified sub-graphs are registered prior to incident auditing.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Proves 5 core theorems (Theorems 1–5) and 3 propositions (Propositions 1–3) and evaluates across three 480-case multi-agent incident corpora (1,440 cases total: 1 development + 2 holdouts), overcoming judge-style attribution baselines that reach only 53.5% agent-level and 14.2% step-level accuracy (pp. 2–6, 22).
Exposed_Security_Function: Author-signed causal message graphs, epoch Merkle commitments, counterfactual replay verification, and certified culpability attribution.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Uses classical digital signatures and Merkle commitments (`STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY`; post-quantum signatures are mentioned only once on p. 38 in related work citing the Aegis Protocol [74]); counterfactual replay requires deterministic or statistically calibrated transition models.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 1–2 (pp. 1–6, Theorems 1–5, Propositions 1–3): 'Every inter-agent message is signed by its author, cites the messages it acts on, and is sealed into an append-only, Merkle-committed record... a rule-following agent is never convicted (Theorem 1). Shifting blame onto such an agent leaves a machine-checkable certificate naming and grading the colluders (Theorem 2)... Destroying evidence yields flagged, author-attributed uncertainty, never a clean acquittal (Theorem 3)...'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: AUDITA seals author-signed, citation-linked inter-agent messages into epoch Merkle logs and proves five theorems (Theorems 1–5) guaranteeing that compliant agents are never convicted, blame-shifting colluders leave machine-checkable certificates, and evidence destruction yields attributed uncertainty rather than acquittal.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 43-page formal auditing and causal attribution paper with complete proofs of Theorems 1–5 and Propositions 1–3 and evaluation across three 480-case multi-agent incident corpora.
Protected_Object: Inter-agent command messages, delivery receipts, epoch Merkle commitments, and post-incident culpability certificates.
Composition_Evidence: Binds signed inter-agent command citations (B2) and actuator execution receipts (B3) to Merkle-sealed counterfactual audit certificates (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-362 / ARXIV-S-0312) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B2;B3;B4); Bukti=THEORETIC_PROOF; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (DG;AD).

Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 1 & Sec. 4 (pp. 2, 6–7, Tables 1–2): 'on GPT-3.5-turbo, the Attack Success Rate (ASR) increased from 48.2% to 84.2%, while the Malicious tool Detection Rate (MDR) was substantially reduced under various settings (reaching as low as 0.3%)... enabling reasoning mode substantially increases ASR: Qwen3-8b rises from 7.44% to 40.5%, and Qwen3-32b from 28.8% to 69.9%.'

Study_Title: MemTrust: A Zero-Trust Architecture for Unified AI Memory System

Enforcement_Point_Location: MemTrust 5-Layer Zero-Trust Unified AI Memory Architecture & TEE Storage/Retrieval Engine.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Confidentiality of unified agent memory against untrusted cloud hosts, cryptographic rollback resistance via TEE-rooted Merkle Hash Trees, and fine-grained cross-agent context delegation.

Performance_Overhead_Reported: Maintains <20% end-to-end throughput overhead (15%–20% on random-access disk I/O due to TEE bounce buffering and Merkle Hash Tree verification, amortized to <8% on sequential log-structured and large vector scan workloads, and ~7% on end-to-end LLM inference pipelines) while eliminating $15K–$50K on-premise server capex (pp. 1–3, 6–8).

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical TEE attestation signatures, AES-256-GCM, and SHA-256 Merkle trees (`STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY`); random-access memory workloads incur 15%–20% bounce-buffering and MHT verification overhead, and TEE side-channel leakage requires ORAM-like mitigations with higher cost (p. 8).
